title: Quality-gate failure record (build-failure)
description: Appended by feature-implementer when the quality gate — the command and verb vocabulary are declared in scripts/layout.toml [gate] — fails. The coordinator reads the latest build-failure record per req_id to decide between retry (retry < 3) and system-design-expert escalation (retry == 3). Append-only; failures are not deleted on success — instead, a build-pass record is appended so the retry trail survives in the file.

retry.description: Retry counter for the retry cycle: the number of build-failure records since the latest design-block, plus one. 1 on the first failure, increments on each subsequent gate failure. Counts build-failure records, not dispatch-starts (which are also written for review-processing and consultation resumes). Resets to 1 after a fresh design-block record (whether the original or a re-triage record with supersedes_record_at set).

failed_check.description: Which step of the quality gate failed. autofix-audit is the gate's doc audit (code-quality-gate § Autofix Audit Procedure); a record failing it carries abort_reason: "design-mismatch" (design-doc-autofix record) or "prd-mismatch" (prd-autofix record) so recovery routes to the owning expert instead of an implementer retry. contracts-sync is the design-doc sync check (code-quality-gate § Design-Doc Sync Procedure); its failure carries abort_reason: "design-mismatch" the same way. conventions-map is the gate's conventions listing (code-quality-gate § Required Checks); its failure is an environment fault (an unresolved base or head, a malformed [conventions] table, a git failure) and carries abort_reason: "prerequisite-missing".

error_output.description: Full error output from the failing command. Multi-line strings are fine; JSONL preserves newlines as \n.

attempted.description: Brief description of the change the implementer made before the failure surfaced.

partial.description: Optional flag set by the implementer when this record is a partial-artifact handoff (the quality-gate run at the dispatch's planned checkpoint came back red). When true, the error_output field carries the gate output and a progress description (which tests pass, which files have been edited, which acceptance criteria remain). The retry counter still ticks; the existing build-failure recovery path routes the next dispatch with the partial-artifact context. Absent or false records carry the default meaning (quality-gate failure).

abort_reason.description: Optional. When set, this record is an abort rather than a retryable failure or a partial-artifact handoff. The implementer declares early (instead of burning the 3-retry cycle) that retrying cannot help: the slice cannot be implemented as triaged, or the gate's autofix audit failed. The handoff-routing skill's Build-Failure Recovery short-circuits past the retry counter when abort_reason is set: wrong-shape-slice → route to product-requirements-expert for re-split; design-mismatch → route to system-design-expert for re-triage; prd-mismatch → route to product-requirements-expert for PRD reconciliation; prerequisite-missing → escalate to human. The implementer SHOULD also set retry to the value it would have set on a normal failure so the retry trail remains coherent. design-mismatch also covers a contracts-sync failure (failed_check: "contracts-sync" — the requirement id missing from the design doc, which only system-design-expert may place) and an autofix-audit failure on a design-doc-autofix record (failed_check: "autofix-audit") — an out-of-bounds or uncovered design-doc change that only system-design-expert may reconcile, since the implementer never modifies docs/. prd-mismatch is the PRD twin — an out-of-bounds prd-autofix record that only product-requirements-expert may reconcile; it is never a mid-loop diagnosis. prerequisite-missing also covers a conventions-map failure (failed_check: "conventions-map"), an environment fault no code edit repairs. Absent means the record is a normal quality-gate failure (or partial-artifact handoff when partial: true).

cycles.description: The red-green-refactor cycles this dispatch ran before it failed the gate or checkpointed. Optional. A slice's total is the sum over its build-pass and build-failure records, so a troubled slice's early dispatches still count toward the slice-size signal's raw input, which nothing reads yet. A dispatch truncated without a record is not counted.
